source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which nutrient stays longest in the stomach?
questions.rationale: Carbohydrates leave in 1–2 hours, proteins 3–4 hours, fats 4–6 hours.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Process of digestion (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: Fats remain in the stomach for 4 to 6 hours

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why do newborns receive vitamin K injection at birth?
options: Breast milk is rich in it
questions.rationale: Vitamin K absorption needs bile and colonic bacteria; newborns lack colonic flora, so an injection prevents bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Large intestines (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Newbom no colonic bacteria Vit. K injection is needed to prevent bleeding

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bulky, fatty, foul-smelling stools (steatorrhea) occur in biliary obstruction because:
questions.rationale: Without bile, fats are not emulsified and pancreatic lipase cannot complete fat digestion.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Process of digestion (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: In biliary obstruction, fats in not emulsified by bile Pancreatic lipase cannot complete digestion of fats.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a stool occult blood (guaiac) test, the client should avoid:
questions.rationale: Red meat, iron, steroids and NSAIDs can cause false or inaccurate results.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Fecal analysis (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: No red meats, poultry. Hemoglobin fibers may be mistaken as blood.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Aling Rosa's child has suspected intestinal worms. How should the nurse send the stool sample for ova and parasites?
questions.rationale: Send a fresh, warm specimen promptly so parasites remain detectable.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Fecal analysis (PDF p. 169)
questions.quote: Stool for Ova and Parasites: Send fresh, warm stool specimen.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a barium swallow, the nurse tells the client:
questions.rationale: Barium causes constipation and white stools for 24–72 hours; give laxative and fluids.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Upper GI series (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: Inform client that stools will be white for 24 —72 hours.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After upper GI endoscopy, which finding suggests perforation?
questions.rationale: Watch for bleeding, crepitus, fever and dyspnea; sore throat is expected.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 UGI endoscopy (PDF p. 171)
questions.quote: Assess: bleeding, crepitus, fever, dyspnea.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During colonoscopy, the client is usually positioned:
questions.rationale: Left lateral with knees flexed eases scope insertion along the colon's anatomy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Colonoscopy (PDF p. 172)
questions.quote: Position: left side, knccs flexed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most accurate way to confirm NGT placement?
questions.rationale: X-ray is most accurate; gastric aspirate pH ≤4–5 also supports placement. Never place the tube end in water.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 NGT insertion (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: X-ray (most accurate)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is NGT insertion length measured?
questions.rationale: Measure from tip of nose to earlobe to xiphoid (NEX), with the client in high Fowler's.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 NGT insertion (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: (tip of the Nose to the tip of the Ear lobe to the Xiphoid process)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During and after tube feeding, the client is kept:
questions.rationale: Elevating the head during and 30–60 minutes after feeding prevents reflux and aspiration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Enteral feeding (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: client should be placed in semi- to high — Fowler's position. To prevent gastric reflux and aspiration.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Tube feeding formula should be given at what temperature?
questions.rationale: Cold formula causes cramping and discomfort; give at room temperature.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Enteral feeding (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: lhe feeding formula should be at room temperature.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A TPN infusion fell 2 hours behind. The nurse should:
options: Keep the rate and notify the doctor
Speed it up to catch up
questions.rationale: Never 'catch up' TPN; rapid infusion causes hyperglycemia and fluid shifts. Notify for recalculation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 TPN (PDF p. 175)
questions.quote: If infusion is delayed, do not "catch up." Notify physician for recalculation of infusion rate.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: If a TPN bag runs out and the next is not ready, the nurse hangs:
questions.rationale: D10W prevents rebound hypoglycemia when hypertonic TPN is interrupted.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 TPN (PDF p. 175)
questions.quote: If TPN administration is interrupted or discontinued, administer DIOW to prevent hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most common complication of TPN?
questions.rationale: Infection is the most common complication; use strict asepsis and change tubing every 24 hours.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 TPN (PDF p. 175)
questions.quote: Infection is the most common complication of TPN.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client has a Sengstaken-Blakemore tube for bleeding varices. Which item must be at the bedside?
questions.rationale: If the gastric balloon ruptures and the tube rises, cut the tube to relieve airway obstruction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Esophageal balloon tamponade (PDF p. 173)
questions.quote: Keep a pair of scissors readily available, as an emergency equipment.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching helps a client with hiatal hernia and reflux?
questions.rationale: Avoid late meals, stay upright after eating, elevate the head of bed and avoid foods that lower LES pressure.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Hiatal hernia (PDF p. 177)
questions.quote: Instruct the client to avoid eating at least 3 hours before bedtime.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which ulcer pain pattern suggests a duodenal ulcer?
options: 2–4 hours after meals, relieved by food
Right after eating, worse with food
questions.rationale: Duodenal pain comes 2–4 hours after meals and at night, eased by food; gastric pain comes soon after eating.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Gastric vs. duodenal ulcer (PDF p. 180)
questions.quote: Pain is relieved by food intake.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Black, tarry stools in a client with a duodenal ulcer indicate:
questions.rationale: Melena is the characteristic sign of bleeding duodenal ulcer; hemorrhage is the most life-threatening complication.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Duodenal ulcer (PDF p. 180)
questions.quote: Characteristic manifestation is melena (black, tarry stool).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client taking a magnesium-based antacid may develop:
questions.rationale: Magnesium antacids cause diarrhea; aluminum antacids cause constipation and low phosphate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Antacids (PDF p. 181)
questions.quote: Magnesium based antacids cause dinrrhcn.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should sucralfate be taken?
questions.rationale: Sucralfate coats ulcers best on an empty stomach and should be separated from antacids.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Cytoprotective drugs (PDF p. 181)
questions.quote: Administer the medication on empty stomach (30 to 60 minutes before meals).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Misoprostol for ulcer prevention is contraindicated in pregnancy because it:
questions.rationale: Misoprostol is an abortifacient prostaglandin analogue.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Prostaglandin analogue (PDF p. 181)
questions.quote: Itis abortifacient, therefore it is contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on metronidazole for H. pylori should avoid:
questions.rationale: Alcohol with metronidazole causes a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, vomiting).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 H. pylori treatment (PDF p. 182)
questions.quote: Advise client to avoid alcohol when on Flagyl therapy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with peptic ulcer drinks a liter of milk daily for relief. The nurse explains that large amounts of milk:
questions.rationale: Milk is alkaline and stimulates rebound HCl secretion; limit it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 PUD nursing interventions (PDF p. 182)
questions.quote: Large quantities of milk (milk is alkaline, thus it stimulates the stomach to increase HCl secretion to neutralize it, causing rebound acidity).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After subtotal gastrectomy, a client feels weak, dizzy and sweaty 15 minutes after eating. This is:
questions.rationale: Early dumping (5–30 min) from rapid hypertonic emptying: weakness, tachycardia, diaphoresis, cramps, diarrhea.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Dumping syndrome (PDF p. 184)
questions.quote: The early signs and symptoms of dumping syndrome occur 5 to 30 minutes after eating.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which advice helps prevent dumping syndrome?
questions.rationale: Small, high-protein, low-sugar meals, fluids between meals and lying down after eating slow gastric emptying.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Dumping syndrome (PDF p. 184)
questions.quote: Instruct client to take fluids after meals or in between meals.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with suspected appendicitis has RLQ pain. Which action is safe?
questions.rationale: Cold relieves pain; heat, enemas and laxatives increase peristalsis and risk rupture.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Appendicitis (PDF p. 185)
questions.quote: Relieve pain by cold application over the abdomen.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Pain at McBurney's point is located:
questions.rationale: McBurney's point is halfway between the umbilicus and right anterior superior iliac spine.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Appendicitis (PDF p. 185)
questions.quote: McBurney's point (halfway between the umbilicus and the anterior spine of the ilium.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with peritonitis is placed in semi-Fowler's to:
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's localizes the inflammatory process in the pelvic cavity and aids breathing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Peritonitis (PDF p. 187)
questions.quote: Bed rest in semi — Fowler's position. To localize inflammatory process in pelvic cavity.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Diverticulitis typically causes pain in the:
questions.rationale: Diverticulitis causes crampy LLQ pain, low-grade fever and altered bowel habits.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Diverticulitis (PDF p. 187)
questions.quote: Crampy abdominal pain in the left, lower quadrant that worsens with movement, coughing or straining.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During an acute diverticulitis flare, the diet is:
questions.rationale: Rest the bowel during flares (NPO then clear liquids); high fiber is for prevention once recovered.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Diverticulitis (PDF p. 188)
questions.quote: NPO, then clear liquids to rest the bowel.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes ulcerative colitis from Crohn's disease?
questions.rationale: UC starts at the rectum and spreads continuously with bloody diarrhea; Crohn's is transmural, patchy, often ileal with fistulas.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Chronic inflammatory bowel disorders (PDF p. 189)
questions.quote: Inflammation starts from the rectum; it ascends until the entire lower colon is affected.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An ileostomy stoma typically drains:
questions.rationale: Ileostomy (RLQ) drains continuous liquid stool and is not irrigated.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Crohn's disease (PDF p. 189)
questions.quote: It has continuous watery fecal drainage. It does not require irrigation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After inguinal hernia repair, the nurse encourages deep breathing but avoids:
questions.rationale: Coughing strains the repair; encourage deep breathing, fluids, and scrotal elevation with ice.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Abdominal hernia (PDF p. 190)
questions.quote: Encourage the client to deep breathe, but not coughing exercises.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A hernia becomes painful with vomiting and distention. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Nausea, vomiting, distention and pain indicate strangulation with compromised blood flow; it is an emergency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Abdominal hernia (PDF p. 190)
questions.quote: Nausea, vomiting, distention, pain indicate strangulated hernia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pencil-shaped stools and tenesmus suggest cancer of the:
questions.rationale: Distal colon and rectal cancer cause ribbon stools, bright red bleeding and tenesmus; right-sided cancer causes occult blood and anemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Colorectal cancer (PDF p. 191)
questions.quote: pencil- or ribbon- shaped stool, tenesmus (involuntary straining at stool)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A new colostomy stoma appears dark purple. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: A healthy stoma is red-pink and moist; dusky or black indicates ischemia and necrosis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Stoma monitoring (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Dark, dusky, or brown black stoma indicates ischemia and necrosis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should an ostomy pouch be emptied?
questions.rationale: Empty at 1/3–1/2 full so the weight doesn't pull off the adhesive and cause leakage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Stoma monitoring (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Empty pouch when it is 1/3 to h full of stool.
